assumptions: The continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio, and PID computations are treated as external plant/controller dynamics; this discrete supervisor model receives the already-computed slip-error input `slp`.
The synthesized root state is named `System` because no explicit summary/root name was provided.
The initial state is `increase` because it is the first state listed in the natural-language FSM description.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: The FSM contains the states `increase`, `hold`, and `decrease`; `increase` sets `k1=1, k2=0, n=0`.
The FSM contains the states `increase`, `hold`, and `decrease`; `hold` neutralizes both valves with `k1=0, k2=0, n=0`.
The FSM contains the states `increase`, `hold`, and `decrease`; `decrease` sets `k1=0, k2=1, n=500` to release pressure.
The transition guards split the slip-error space into four bands using `slp` thresholds.
`increase` and `hold` set `n=0`; `decrease` sets `n=500` to release pressure.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init verifies the initial transition lands in increase with inlet valve active, then slp above 0.01 keeps increase from taking its slp<=0.01 transition.
scenario_results.name: default_init_to_increase_and_positive_no_fire

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes the inclusive increase->hold guard at slp=0.01 and verifies hold neutralizes both valves.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes hold->increase when slp is just above 0.01 and verifies increase commands k1=1, k2=0, n=0.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_positive_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes hold->decrease when slp is just below -0.01 and verifies decrease releases pressure with k2=1 and n=500.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes that hold does not enter decrease at the exclusive slp<-0.01 boundary when slp equals -0.01.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_decrease_at_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes the inclusive decrease->hold guard at slp=-0.01 and verifies hold neutralizes the return valve and pump.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_negative_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies the deadband behavior in hold for slp=0.0: neither increase nor decrease transition should fire and valves stay neutral.
scenario_results.name: hold_deadband_no_fire_at_zero_slip

evidence: NL: increase sets k1=1, k2=0, n=0; hold sets k1=0, k2=0, n=0; decrease sets k1=0, k2=1, n=500.
DSL: state increase/hold/decrease enter actions assign the same k1, k2, n values.
NL guards: increase->hold slp <= 0.01; hold->increase slp > 0.01; hold->decrease slp < -0.01; decrease->hold slp >= -0.01.
DSL contains the same four guarded transitions.
findings.summary: The DSL faithfully captures the three-state ABS hydraulic supervisor described in the NL, including the increase/hold/decrease states, valve/pump assignments, and four slip-error threshold guards.

evidence: NL says wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute slip ratio and that a PID-based slip controller drives the supervisor.
DSL exposes only slp, k1, k2, and n; it does not model wheel speed, vehicle speed, slip-ratio computation, PID state, PID gains, or PID output.
Grounding assumptions narrow the model to a discrete supervisor receiving already-computed slp as an external input.
findings.summary: Coverage is strong for the discrete Stateflow-style supervisor but incomplete for the broader coupled PID/slip-computation context mentioned in the NL.

evidence: NL: 'three-state FSM coupled with a PID-based slip controller'
NL: 'Wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute the slip ratio'
DSL: no variables or transitions for wheel speed, vehicle speed, PID integral/derivative terms, PID output, or slip-ratio calculation.
NL final sentence states continuous wheel-slip dynamics remain in the plant model, supporting a supervisor-only interpretation.
findings.summary: If the intended target is the full paper-level ABS regulator, the PID and slip-ratio computation are absent; if the target is only the discrete supervisor, this gap is acceptable and explicitly scoped.

evidence: Design diagnostics: W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for slp.
Design diagnostics: W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for k1, k2, n.
design_diagnostics_summary.nl_external_input_vars includes slp.
external_input_role_ledger identifies slp as an external_input_candidate.
NL describes k1, k2, and n as valve/pump actions rather than guard-driving internal variables.
findings.summary: Static diagnostics report slp as read but unwritten and k1/k2/n as unreferenced by guards, but these are consistent with slp being an external input and k1/k2/n being pure actuator outputs.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary: n_states_leaf=3, n_transitions_normal=5, n_variables=4, action_count=3.
Grounding map covers all three states, all three enter actions, all four normal transitions, and all four guards with high confidence.
sim_summary: 7 scenarios passed out of 7, including positive boundary, negative boundary, deadband, and actuator-output checks.
design_diagnostics_summary.ok=true with blocking_count=0.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate for the discrete supervisor scope. No quality cap is warranted for missing states, transitions, guards, or actions because the required FSM elements are present and simulated across threshold boundaries.

evidence: sim_summary includes scenarios for increase->hold at slp=0.01, hold->increase above 0.01, hold->decrease below -0.01, decrease->hold at -0.01, and hold deadband at zero slip.
No simulation failures or setup errors are reported.
The scenarios do not evaluate wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, or PID dynamics.
findings.summary: Path-1 evaluation risk is low for the discrete FSM because simulations exercise each specified transition and boundary condition; risk remains only if the oracle is expected to validate continuous/PID behavior.

evidence: Grounding map confidence is 0.98-0.99 for states, actions, transitions, and guards.
Grounding source_summary assumes the discrete supervisor receives already-computed slip-error input slp.
The NL mentions PID output and slip-ratio computation, which are not decomposed into separate grounded model elements.
findings.summary: Path-2 grounding risk is low for the FSM elements but moderate for the scope assumption that slp fully represents the external PID/slip-error signal.
